model_rule: NEVER hardcode project specifics into the framework — framework (packages/) is generic, projects (examples/) are specific

findings.gap: Project-specific example name 'cinematic-video-production' is hardcoded in framework prompt templates across three files in packages/core/src/planning/. The framework should use configurable or placeholder references, not bake in a specific example project name.
findings.evidence: analyze.ts:244 — examples/cinematic-video-production/.converge/playbooks/default/tasks/02-cast/001-extract/TASK.md; implement-executable.ts:111 — same path; task-md-schema.ts:82 — same path; task-md-schema.ts:8 — 'examples/cinematic-video-production/'
findings.correction: Replace hardcoded example paths with a generic placeholder (e.g. {example_reference_path}) or read from project configuration. Add a test that greps for project-specific names in packages/core/src/planning/.
findings.test_to_write: tests/planning/prompt-templates.test.ts — grep all files in packages/core/src/planning/ for 'cinematic-video-production'; test fails if any match found

findings.gap: TASK.md discovery glob patterns (.converge/epics/**, .converge/playbooks/**) are hardcoded as string literals instead of being derived from StoragePaths or a central path registry.
findings.evidence: validate.ts:158-161 — four hardcoded glob patterns as array literals in validateProject()
findings.correction: Derive glob patterns from the StoragePaths interface or a central directory-structure config rather than inline string literals.
findings.test_to_write: tests/validation/path-configurability.test.ts — verify that changing StoragePaths.playbooks updates validation discovery patterns
